depiction.primary_object: wireless signal fan with three arcs above a dot
modifiers: exclamation mark on the bottom right
depiction.composition: single icon with bottom-right status badge

readings.meaning: Wi-Fi problem, unstable internet, or network connection error
weak wireless signal or dead zone

ambiguity: At very small sizes the exclamation mark can blend into the right side of the Wi-Fi arcs or look like a lock or question mark badge.

modifier_semantics.meaning: error, warning, problem, or disconnected state

Ask landlord if the router in the hallway was moved or unplugged again
Try forgetting the network and renewing the DHCP lease on the iPad

reasoning: Shows a standard three-arc Wi-Fi symbol with an exclamation mark badge on the lower right, universally understood as a Wi-Fi problem, unstable connection, or internet outage. It fits a narrow but common family of household and office troubleshooting tasks (fixing dropouts, calling the ISP, resolving dead zones), though it can be confused at small sizes with plain Wi-Fi or other badged Wi-Fi variants.
